title: Debug: Single-Port RAM
constraints: Intended behavior: 16 × 8-bit synchronous RAM. Everything happens on a rising edge with `en = 1`: if `we`, write `wdata` to `addr`.
Registered read, **write-first**: on an enabled edge `rdata` becomes `mem[addr]`, or the new `wdata` if this edge writes it. With `en = 0`, `rdata` holds.
No reset (uninitialized words are don't-care until written). The starter has **2 bugs**.
hints: Write 16 different values to addresses 0 … 15 and read them all back. Which addresses collide?
Write and read the same address on the same edge. Which value comes out?
FPGA block RAMs support read-first, write-first and no-change modes. The spec asks for write-first.

examples.title: full address range
examples.expected: each word keeps its own value
